theme: The Legacy: The Rise and Fall of Yawgmoth (Thran to Apocalypse)
status: FINISHED STORY-FIRST PROPOSAL — intentionally Rule 0 (Commander-banned story cards included); not yet approved or locked by Cory

beats.title: I. The Thran: Yawgmoth claims Phyrexia

cards.name: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician
cards.why: Yawgmoth before his ascension: the Thran healer and tyrant who becomes Phyrexia's master.

cards.name: Rebbec, Architect of Ascension
cards.why: Thran architect and Glacian's wife; her choices help seal the portal against Yawgmoth.

cards.name: Glacian, Powerstone Engineer
cards.why: The Thran inventor whose powerstone legacy shapes the brothers' discovery and later artifacts.

cards.name: Fall of the Thran
cards.why: The Saga's title and chapters depict the collapse of the civilization Yawgmoth exploits.

beats.title: II. The Brothers' War: the stones, Gix and the Sylex

cards.name: Tocasia, Dig Site Mentor
cards.why: Urza and Mishra's mentor at the excavation that precedes their destructive rivalry.

cards.name: Mightstone
cards.why: The original Antiquities printing's flavor records Urza finding his half of the powerstone with Tocasia at the Hall of Tagsin; this is an actual primary-text story page.

cards.name: Weakstone
cards.why: The original Antiquities printing's flavor records Mishra discovering his half of the powerstone, making the brothers' split tangible.

cards.name: Splitting the Powerstone
cards.why: A literal card depiction of the brothers dividing the ancient stone.

cards.name: Urza, Lord Protector
cards.why: The elder brother's card is one half of the Urza-Planeswalker meld with the Mightstone and Weakstone.

cards.name: Mishra, Claimed by Gix
cards.why: The younger brother's Phyrexian corruption; melds with the Dragon Engine as Mishra Lost to Phyrexia.

cards.name: The Mightstone and Weakstone
cards.why: The original divided powerstone, also Urza's meld component.

cards.name: Ashnod, Flesh Mechanist
cards.why: Mishra's artificer and a central architect of the war's living-machinery horror.

cards.name: Tawnos, Urza's Apprentice
cards.why: Urza's apprentice, showing the human hands behind Urza's machinery.

cards.name: Queen Kayla bin-Kroog
cards.why: Kayla's account of the conflict preserved the history of the brothers' war.

cards.name: Gix, Yawgmoth Praetor
cards.why: The Phyrexian manipulator who corrupts Mishra and ties the war to Yawgmoth.

cards.name: Phyrexian Dragon Engine
cards.why: Mishra's mechanized fate; the paired meld card that makes the fall playable on the table.

cards.name: The Brothers' War
cards.why: A Saga that recounts the central conflict rather than an unrelated efficient spell.

cards.name: The Antiquities War
cards.why: A historical Saga linking Urza and Mishra's war to the later surviving account.

cards.name: Golgothian Sylex
cards.why: The original Antiquities printing of the ancient device that ends the Brothers' War on Argoth; complements the later card Urza's Sylex.

cards.name: Urza's Sylex
cards.why: The weapon detonated on Argoth at the end of the Brothers' War.

cards.name: Brotherhood's End
cards.why: The climax of the brothers' conflict and the world-altering destruction.

beats.title: III. Urza's long war: Karn, Xantcha, Serra and the Legacy

cards.name: Karn, Silver Golem
cards.why: Urza's silver golem, friend and the sentient keeper of the Legacy.

cards.name: Xantcha, Sleeper Agent
cards.why: The Phyrexian sleeper who becomes Urza's companion and helps him understand his enemy.

cards.name: Barrin, Master Wizard
cards.why: Urza's collaborator at the Tolarian Academy, shaping the long war.

cards.name: Teferi, Temporal Archmage
cards.why: Urza's Tolarian student and the time mage whose decisions shape the invasion era; this card depicts the character in later life.

cards.name: Jhoira, Weatherlight Captain
cards.why: Jhoira helped connect Tolarian artifice to the Weatherlight and was the ship's first captain; this card is a later depiction.

cards.name: Serra the Benevolent
cards.why: Serra created the realm whose white mana later powered the Weatherlight.

cards.name: Planar Collapse
cards.why: The destruction of Serra's Realm, transformed into power for the Weatherlight's planar engine.

cards.name: Power Matrix
cards.why: Its Mercadian Masques printing's flavor quotes Karn; a machine-fitting glimpse of the Legacy's guardian.

cards.name: Heartstone
cards.why: The Sliver Queen's heartstone and Legacy-object imagery connect Rath's slivers with Urza's weapon.

cards.name: Urza, Lord High Artificer
cards.why: Urza in his long-term role as architect of the anti-Phyrexian Legacy and artifacts.

cards.name: Gate to Phyrexia
cards.why: Jarsyl's Antiquities-era diary flavor records a later entry into Phyrexia; this is a witness to the plane, not necessarily Rebbec's original portal.

cards.name: Yawgmoth's Bargain
cards.why: Urza's Destiny-era emblem of how Yawgmoth trades life for power; a thematic expression, not a claim of a single documented personal contract. Banned in Commander, intentionally included for story-first Rule 0.

cards.name: Yawgmoth's Will
cards.why: The Urza's Saga spell named directly for Yawgmoth's inexorable will; no flavor line needed for the unmistakable historical reference.

beats.title: IV. The Weatherlight crew: Rath, betrayal and the Legacy's recovery

cards.name: Captain Sisay
cards.why: The original Weatherlight captain seeks the scattered Legacy; a second, period-specific Sisay printing distinct from the commander.

cards.name: Gerrard Capashen
cards.why: The Legacy's destined human champion and original Weatherlight saga protagonist.

cards.name: Hanna, Ship's Navigator
cards.why: The Weatherlight navigator and artificer keeping the ship and the search together.

cards.name: Squee, Goblin Nabob
cards.why: The crew's iconic goblin, whose immortality becomes part of the saga.

cards.name: Mirri, Cat Warrior
cards.why: The Weatherlight's fighter whose fate is tied to Crovax and the mission.

cards.name: Tahngarth, Talruum Hero
cards.why: The crew's minotaur warrior, changed by imprisonment and Phyrexian violence.

cards.name: Orim, Samite Healer
cards.why: The Weatherlight's medic, representing care and sacrifice amid the war.

cards.name: Predator, Flagship
cards.why: The Phyrexian ship pursuing the Weatherlight across Rath.

cards.name: Crovax the Cursed
cards.why: The Weatherlight ally who falls into vampirism and ultimately serves the enemy.

cards.name: Ertai, the Corrupted
cards.why: The former Weatherlight mage turned into a Phyrexian opponent.

cards.name: Volrath the Fallen
cards.why: The villainous evincar of Rath, linked to Sisay's abduction and the Legacy's dispersal.

cards.name: Eladamri, Lord of Leaves
cards.why: The Skyshroud resistance leader who joins the fight against Rath's masters.

cards.name: Skyship Weatherlight
cards.why: The original story's ship, and one of the physical artifacts connected to the Legacy.

cards.name: Sliver Queen
cards.why: Her heartstone is a key point in Karn's compassionate recovery of a Legacy component.

cards.name: Rofellos, Llanowar Emissary
cards.why: A member of the original Weatherlight crew; his death matters to the crew's history. Banned in Commander, intentionally included for story-first Rule 0.

cards.name: Starke of Rath
cards.why: A member of the original Weatherlight expedition whose self-serving betrayals help tell the Rath chapter; his Tempest flavor is about loyalty.

cards.name: Multani, Maro-Sorcerer
cards.why: The Yavimayan nature spirit and Weatherlight-era ally; the Urza's Legacy printing directly addresses Urza in its flavor line.

cards.name: Commander Greven il-Vec
cards.why: The Predator's commander and a direct Weatherlight antagonist; his Tempest card and quote make the Rath conflict concrete.

beats.title: V. Invasion to Apocalypse: Yawgmoth's end

cards.name: Tsabo Tavoc
cards.why: A central Phyrexian general in the invasion of Dominaria, giving the invading army a named commander.

cards.name: Urza Assembles the Titans
cards.why: The Nine Titans are Urza's planeswalker strike force during the Phyrexian Invasion; their mustering belongs beside the final assault, not in the earlier Tolarian preparations.

cards.name: Tevesh Szat, Doom of Fools
cards.why: One of Urza's Nine Titans whose treachery helps explain why the plan to invade Phyrexia fell apart.

cards.name: Freyalise, Llanowar's Fury
cards.why: The great green planeswalker and a member of Urza's Nine Titans; a necessary Coalition-side participant.

cards.name: Lord Windgrace
cards.why: The ancient planeswalker and member of the Nine Titans; later key to Urborg's protection.

cards.name: Commodore Guff
cards.why: The eccentric planeswalker and one of the Nine Titans who strike Phyrexia during the Invasion.

cards.name: Yawgmoth's Agenda
cards.why: Yawgmoth's sweeping objectives as the Invasion approaches.

cards.name: Urza's Guilt
cards.why: The Planeshift card's printed quote connects Urza's internal conflict to Yawgmoth and the war.

cards.name: Phyrexian Altar
cards.why: Invasion-era printing explicitly invokes Yawgmoth and Phyrexia's sacrifice cult.

cards.name: Death Grasp
cards.why: An Apocalypse-era card with printed Yawgmoth flavor, explicitly portraying the cruelty of his campaign.

cards.name: Pernicious Deed
cards.why: An Apocalypse-era permanent with Yawgmoth's flavor text and destructive design.

cards.name: Jilt
cards.why: Apocalypse-era flavor mentions Yawgmoth and Gerrard, directly tying enemies and hero.

cards.name: Vindicate
cards.why: The Apocalypse-era card depicts the conflict's bitter moral stakes; printing flavor must be checked before finalizing.

cards.name: Heroes' Reunion
cards.why: Invasion printing contains a Gerrard line and depicts reunification against the invaders.

cards.name: Legacy Weapon
cards.why: The completed artifact culmination of Urza's long design and the Weatherlight crew's quest.

cards.name: Coalition Victory
cards.why: The five-color united defense of Dominaria against the invasion, and a fitting story ending.

beats.title: VI. Historical ground: Thran ruins, warfronts, Rath and Dominaria

cards.name: Thran Portal
cards.why: The ancient Thran portals are central to Yawgmoth's access to Phyrexia; this is a later retrospective card.

cards.name: Hall of Tagsin
cards.why: The buried Thran archaeological site underlying the brothers' discovery.

cards.name: Caves of Koilos
cards.why: The site where the brothers found and divided the powerstone; its Dominaria United flavor is later Phyrexian-return foreshadowing, not a contemporaneous Brothers' War quote.

cards.name: Tocasia's Dig Site
cards.why: The dig that brought Urza and Mishra under Tocasia's instruction.

cards.name: Mishra's Factory
cards.why: Mishra's war production, first represented in Antiquities.

cards.name: Mishra's Workshop
cards.why: The original Antiquities factory with flavor involving Mishra and Tocasia; closer to the actual Brothers' War than a later Foundry.

cards.name: Urza's Mine
cards.why: Urza's mining network and artifact-war supply; choose an early historical printing.

cards.name: Urza's Power Plant
cards.why: Urza's industrial power network from the original Antiquities story set.

cards.name: Urza's Tower
cards.why: Urza's tower network and archetypal Antiquities-era war infrastructure.

cards.name: Argoth, Sanctum of Nature
cards.why: Argoth, whose destruction ends the Brothers' War and brings an Ice Age.

cards.name: Tolarian Academy
cards.why: The actual academy where Urza, Barrin, Teferi, Jhoira and Karn's stories intersect; the Urza's Saga printing references temporal disaster. Banned in Commander, intentionally included for Rule 0.

cards.name: Serra's Sanctum
cards.why: Serra's sanctuary, before Phyrexian corruption and the plane's collapse fuel the Weatherlight.

cards.name: Volrath's Stronghold
cards.why: The stronghold on Rath housing the captives and opposition to the Weatherlight.

cards.name: Phyrexian Tower
cards.why: A Phyrexian stronghold; the chosen later printing quotes Karn reflecting on Yawgmoth's death, so its flavor is a retrospective epilogue.

cards.name: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth
cards.why: Yawgmoth's ominous resting-place and a future retrospective of the aftermath of Apocalypse.

cards.name: Battlefield Forge
cards.why: An Apocalypse-era battlefield land; atmospheric rather than proof of a specific named battle.

cards.name: Llanowar Wastes
cards.why: Llanowar's threatened territory and the woodlands' role in Dominaria's resistance.

cards.name: Coastal Tower
cards.why: An Invasion-set Dominarian defensive landscape and two-color source.

cards.name: Elfhame Palace
cards.why: An Invasion-set woodland settlement associated with the coalition era.

cards.name: Kor Haven
cards.why: The Rath/Kor resistance setting in Nemesis, connecting the Weatherlight journey with places of refuge.

playability.name: Phyrexian Lens
playability.why: Colored-mana generation from an Invasion-set artifact with Gerrard-era flavor.

notes: Built as a 100-card historical exhibit and not a tournament-legal or normal Commander-list recommendation.
Three banned cards intentionally retained at the user's instruction: Rofellos, Llanowar Emissary; Yawgmoth's Bargain; Tolarian Academy.
Color identity is WUBRG through Sisay, Weatherlight Captain; all other singleton rules retained.
Story chapters are historical and may cite retrospective depictions; printed eras and flavor are independently audited.
The Lore-based Yawgmoth deck is independent of the 62 locked Grixis Commander Encyclopedia decks.
